domain: Historical Sociology / Legal Anthropology / Commitment Systems
topic_summary: Analysis of dueling's disappearance as a legitimate honor-settlement mechanism in Western societies (roughly 1600-1900). The topic is flagged as a contested kernel: whether dueling's decline represents a drop (practice fell to fringe but remained thinkable), a contraction (became structurally unthinkable), or an overdetermined composite where both mechanisms operated simultaneously.

key_entities: Dueling practice (formalized violence for honor restoration)
State monopoly on violence (Weberian legitimacy claim)
key_tensions: Private violence vs state monopoly (duelists vs legal authority)
Aristocratic honor vs bourgeois respectability (competing status systems)
Formal prohibition vs informal tolerance (law vs enforcement practice)
mechanisms: Legal prosecution: anti-dueling statutes with variable enforcement
Status substitution: alternative honor frameworks (professional reputation, wealth display)
Economic liability: insurance exclusions, inheritance complications for duelists
absences: Absence of systematic data on enforcement rates vs statute passage dates
Absence of cross-class comparison (aristocratic vs merchant dueling decline trajectories)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: Honor as requiring violent defense when publicly challenged
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: Peer recognition within status group; no formal adjudicator
commitment_system_recognition.candidate_pattern: Type 2 (Interpretive Drift) transitioning to Type 4 (Covert Revision)

readings.commitment: Dueling remained structurally legitimate but became practically rare due to external costs
readings.authority_grounding: Honor code persisted; state prosecution raised costs without delegitimizing the practice itself
readings.expected_structural_delta: Practice frequency drops but conceptual availability remains; dueling remains thinkable as honor mechanism

readings.commitment: Dueling became structurally unthinkable as honor itself was redefined to exclude violence
readings.authority_grounding: Bourgeois respectability norms replaced aristocratic honor; violence became incompatible with status
readings.expected_structural_delta: Conceptual space contracts; dueling exits the set of legitimate honor responses

readings.commitment: Overdetermined decline: external costs (drop) and conceptual redefinition (contraction) operated simultaneously
readings.authority_grounding: Both state prosecution AND status-system transformation; non-break composite with contraction edge
readings.expected_structural_delta: Two mechanisms with different victim sets and extractiveness profiles; contraction edge makes drop mechanism insufficient alone

omegas.description: Systematic data on enforcement rates vs statute passage dates is absent. If enforcement lagged statutes by decades, drop mechanism weakens; if enforcement was immediate, drop mechanism strengthens. Contraction reading less sensitive to this gap.

Absence of cross-class comparison data. If merchant/bourgeois dueling declined earlier than aristocratic dueling, contraction reading strengthens (status-norm shift precedes legal enforcement). If decline was synchronous across classes, drop reading strengthens (external costs dominated).

Does composite_reading collapse into one of its components, or do drop and contraction have genuinely different victim sets and epsilon profiles? If contraction edge is load-bearing (drop alone insufficient), composite is real. If contraction merely accelerates drop, readings collapse.

Analysis restricted to Western European/North American contexts. Non-Western honor-violence systems (e.g., Japanese samurai dueling, Ottoman honor codes) may exhibit different drop/contraction dynamics. Generalization beyond Western bourgeois state formation is omega variable.
omegas.source: Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) + domain boundary recognition

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Kernel decomposition is structurally valid: three readings emit different constraints (different victim sets, different epsilon bins, different beneficiaries). Composite reading tests whether mechanisms are genuinely independent or collapse. Enforcement data gap and cross-class trajectory absence are bounded as omegas rather than fractures.
